newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil hit by weaker futures, mild weather.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil hit by weaker futures, mild weather.

text.p: NWE gas oil business was quietened on Monday as the market digested firmer and then weaker futures amid continued mild weather.
March IPE gas oil lost $2.25 a tonne to close at $160.25, pressured lower by weaker NYMEX heating oil and gasoline.
Barge premiums actually firmed by 50 cents or so, limiting the extremes of the futures fall and a couple of refinery material barges were sold at March IPE +50 cents fob Rotterdam.
On the cargo side, Russian premiums were maintained at around March IPE -50 cents cif ARA.
"Some support is coming from people looking to buy in order to work something eastwards," said one dealer.
At least one 70kt cargo found a ship last week to head to the Far East.
But, there remains concern of the large amounts of gas oil seen available in the ARA region.
"The market is wondering what is going to happen to the large Feb gas oil delivery and the estimated 100,000-200,000 tonnes of Russian done into ARA last week," said one trader.
"It's not the ugly sister of gas oil, it's worse than that," said one trader.
"There just is not the demand," said another.
Premiums were notionally assessed steady at around screen flat although offers were heard as high as March IPE +$1 and +$1.50 cif NWE.
Diesel cargo premiums were also broadly steady around March IPE +$13 cif NWE.
